stem: An obstetric emergency team has been activated for a rapidly deteriorating client. Which team practice best supports a safe, coordinated response?

options.A: Assign explicit roles and use a standardized emergency-communication process so assessment, medications, equipment, and escalation tasks are coordinated.
options.B: Allow every team member to choose tasks independently without a shared role structure because predefined responsibilities slow emergency care.
options.C: Avoid standardized communication tools during the event because structured communication increases confusion under stress.
options.D: Have only one clinician perform all urgent tasks until the diagnosis is confirmed, then involve the rest of the team.

rationale: A is correct. ACOG guidance on preparation for obstetric and gynecologic emergencies recommends protocols that designate team-member roles, drills and ongoing training, and formal standardized emergency communication such as SBAR. Clear roles and structured communication improve coordination during time-critical events and support rapid-response effectiveness. B and C remove the structure intended to reduce communication and task failures. D underuses the interprofessional response and can delay simultaneous urgent actions.
educational_objective: Use clearly assigned emergency roles and standardized communication to coordinate simultaneous interprofessional actions during an obstetric emergency.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
source_document_title: Preparing for Clinical Emergencies in Obstetrics and Gynecology
source_locator: Early Warning Systems/Rapid Response Team — protocols should designate team-member roles; drills and ongoing training should be implemented; formal standardized communication such as SBAR can optimize emergency response; teamwork and communication increase efficiency/effectiveness
source_claim_supported: Structured obstetric emergency response should include designated roles and standardized communication so interprofessional tasks are coordinated efficiently during time-critical events.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; communicate with the interprofessional team, assign/coordinate responsibilities, and implement emergency response systems
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — role clarity and standardized communication during obstetric emergencies
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source abstract statement into an applied team-coordination decision. The final item uses directly supported ACOG emergency-response elements—designated roles and standardized communication—rather than vague claims that structure is simply ‘important’ or universally improves every outcome.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.clinical_category: obstetric emergency teamwork / role assignment / communication
audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ACOG emergency-preparedness guidance. Role designation, drills/training, and standardized communication are explicit components of effective emergency systems.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A stays within directly supported teamwork processes and does not claim that a specific proprietary team model is mandatory. No unsupported closed-loop terminology or staffing ratio is introduced.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; explicit roles and structured communication coordinate simultaneous emergency tasks.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; unstructured task selection increases risk of duplication, omission, and delay.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; ACOG supports standardized communication rather than avoiding it.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; obstetric emergencies require coordinated interprofessional action, not sequential solo performance of all urgent tasks.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A reflects the organized team structure recommended by ACOG.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address team organization during the same emergency rather than unrelated clinical treatment.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care is directly aligned because the item tests interprofessional coordination and communication during emergency response.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked role-designation wording, standardized communication evidence, avoidance of unsupported outcome claims, SBAR example versus mandate, parallel-task rationale, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
